headline: New evening confusion since about mid-October, including a stove left on, has no documented work-up result yet, and his caregiver Robert is exhausted and asking for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-11-02 Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit that week. The record shows no results or visit after that, and no encounters in the period.
items.verifier_note: Note matches: two weeks evening confusion, stove once, oriented to person/place not date, no fever, plan UA, med review, PCP visit this week. Encounters record is empty, supporting 'no encounters'; no results are in the cited sources.

items.statement: On 2026-11-22 Robert, his grandson and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group. Evenings are also when the confusion has been reported.
items.verifier_note: Social work note supports all details (grandson/primary caregiver, exhaustion, poor sleep, evenings alone worry, respite request, options and support group discussed). Evening confusion is supported by the 11-02 nursing note.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 2026-09-29 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly. The notes do not show whether the walker, home evaluation or grab bars were put in place.
items.verifier_note: PT findings and recommendations match the note. However, the statement says the PT evaluation was in the cited note of 2026-09-29, which is correct, but the claim that the notes don't show implementation is an absence claim; the fall on Sep 25 is omitted but not contradicted. The core is supported, yet 'PT twice weekly' is described as a recommendation while the note says 'Will see twice weekly' (PT's own plan). Minor wording mismatch.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which started 2026-08-01. The last flu vaccine was given 2026-06-30.
items.verifier_note: Immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season false, season start 2026-08-01, and most recent flu vaccine 2026-06-30.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 2026-11-02 completed, and what did they show?
Is the evening confusion and stove incident prompting a home safety or cognitive assessment, and does the stove need a safety measure?
What respite and evening support can be arranged for Robert, and how soon?
Has the walker been delivered, and have the home safety evaluation and grab bar installation been done?
Should the flu vaccine be offered now for this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any readmissions, with reason for visit.

Cardiac events: look for chest pain, angina episodes, or nitroglycerin spray use since the ischemic heart disease diagnosis (2026-06-30) and metoprolol, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin, and simvastatin starts (2026-07-07). Check for any ECG, troponin, cath, or cardiology referral, and any bleeding or bruising on clopidogrel.

Medication reconciliation: compare the five active medications against the prior list. Confirm that metoprolol, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin, simvastatin, and alendronate are all still being taken and are filled on time. Flag any stops, dose changes, or new PRN opioid, muscle relaxant, or migraine medication.

Substance use and controlled-substance safety: review the dependent drug abuse diagnosis (2018). Check for any new or refilled controlled prescriptions, early refill requests, pharmacy or prescriber changes, urine drug screens, naloxone availability, relapse signs, and whether the team is aware of any use since the last review.

Pain and migraine: track chronic pain and intractable migraine frequency, severity, and rescue medication use over the window. Check for any headache-related ED visits, and whether pain scores or pain-interference measures changed.

Falls and fracture risk: check for falls, near-falls, or injuries. Osteoporosis is documented and alendronate started 2026-06-30, so confirm the administration instructions (fasting, upright 30 minutes) are being followed, check for dental or jaw problems, and review any new fracture or bone density follow-up. The scoliosis history also matters for mobility and balance.

Vitals and weight: review blood pressure and heart rate trends, especially after starting metoprolol (watch for low HR, dizziness, or hypotension). Review the weight trend against obesity (BMI 30+) history and any new edema or shortness of breath.
Dental: impacted molars are on the problem list. Check for dental pain, extraction or oral surgery plans, and any dental visits that would require bisphosphonate timing review with alendronate.

Function, ADLs, and cognition: compare ADL and IADL status against the prior review, including mobility, transfers, and driving if relevant. Check any cognitive screen or change in medication management. Confirm whether he can manage his own medications and the new cardiac regimen.

Mood, attendance, and caregiver: review mood screens, attendance at PACE day services and appointments, transportation barriers, caregiver or family status changes, and any care-plan items that are due or overdue in the window (reassessments, care-plan signatures, and the review-date deadline of 2026-11-30).
